A0228.title: Robot Debug Interface Hardening
A0228.definition: Closing or encrypting production debug & maintenance interfaces, enforcing BLE provisioning authentication, removing vendor-SDK hardcoded credentials, and minimizing maintenance-port exposure to prevent attackers from gaining device control via debug channels.
A0228.description: Robotic debug interface hardening targets attack vectors such as BLE provisioning command injection, hardcoded keys, and unsecured debug UARTs that grant root access (e.g., Unitree UniPwn CVE-2025-35027), converging the attack surface across four layers. First, disable JTAG/UART debug interfaces in production or enforce strong authentication to prevent physical access from directly yielding a shell. Second, enforce mutual authentication and per-device unique keys on BLE provisioning interfaces, removing hardcoded encryption keys shared across all devices. Third, remove hardcoded credentials and backdoor services from vendor SDKs (such as pre-installed remote access like CloudSail), scanning and cleaning before factory shipment. Fourth, minimize exposure of maintenance ports, retaining only essential maintenance functions and recording operational audit logs. This measure works in conjunction with A0109 (IoT device strong authentication and default credential changes), A0117 (default credential scanning and auto-remediation), and A0114 (IoT device security configuration enforcement); the former focus on generic device authentication, while this measure specifically addresses robotics-unique debug and provisioning interfaces.
A0228.limitation: There is a conflict between maintenance convenience and security: after hardening, on-site debugging requires additional authentication steps, increasing operational costs. Legacy device firmware cannot be upgraded, leaving residual vulnerabilities unpatched. BLE provisioning authentication may impact the first-time provisioning user experience. Some vendors resist removing backdoor services for the sake of remote maintenance convenience.
